Horticalc 0.6.3 adds a conventional Windows installer while retaining the
portable ZIP, gives blocked portable downloads a clear Mark-of-the-Web
diagnostic, and incorporates the confirmed application, data, and dependency
updates accumulated since 0.6.2. Public API routes, CLI commands, and persisted
profile formats remain compatible.

## Windows installer and portable ZIP

- The recommended Windows artifact is now
  `horticalc-v0.6.3-windows-setup.exe`. It installs for the current user under
  `%LocalAppData%\Programs\Horticalc`, adds a Start-menu entry and uninstaller,
  and requires no administrator rights.
- The portable `horticalc-v0.6.3-windows.zip` remains fully supported.
- Installer upgrades replace only shipped program files. Both upgrade and
  uninstall preserve `user/`; uninstall removes runtime logs.
- The setup, ZIP, and their SHA-256 files receive GitHub Artifact Attestations.
  The Windows setup and executable are not Authenticode-signed, so Windows can
  still display an unknown-publisher warning.

## Mark of the Web recovery

Windows can propagate Internet-zone metadata from a downloaded ZIP to the
bundled `Python.Runtime.dll`. Before importing the API, starting the server, or
opening WebView2, the packaged Windows GUI now detects Internet and Restricted
zone values and exits with the exact portable recovery steps. Horticalc never
removes the metadata or weakens Windows security settings automatically.

For the portable ZIP, use **Properties → Unblock → Apply** before extracting.
If it was already extracted while blocked, back up `user/`, delete the affected
extraction, unblock the original ZIP, and extract it again. The setup installer
does not propagate its own download mark to installed runtime files.

## Confirmed UI work

- Preferences, supported locales, Solver presentation and printable output,
  water handling, theme behavior, and frontend resource loading now use the
  confirmed API-owned configuration paths.
- Frontend localization cache handling and the related serving, theme,
  launcher, and preference coverage were refreshed.

## Data corrections

- EPSO Microtop now correctly contributes boron rather than molybdenum; the
  official composition reference is recorded with the product data.
- Fertilizer CSV records were normalized to the canonical 24-column schema.
- The default reference recipe now starts at zero-percent reverse osmosis.

## Dependency maintenance

- PyInstaller 6.22.0 is used for release packaging.
- Uvicorn 0.52.3 and Starlette 1.6.0 are used in the constrained release
  environment.
- The frontend development lockfile includes the patched `js-yaml` 4.3.1,
  `brace-expansion` 5.0.9, and `nanoid` 3.3.18 releases.
- Previously merged maintenance updates include Packaging 26.3 and the current
  attestation action revision.

## Verification and upgrade notes

The release workflow builds and smoke-tests the Windows and Linux onedir
packages. The Windows job additionally compiles the installer, marks it as an
Internet download, verifies that the installed runtime is unmarked and healthy,
reinstalls across a user-data sentinel, and verifies uninstall cleanup. Linux
GUI compatibility remains gated on Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, Debian 13, and Fedora 44.

Existing portable users should back up `user/` before replacing an extraction.
Installer users can install 0.6.3 over an earlier setup build; their `user/`
directory remains in place. Windows 10/11 requires Microsoft WebView2 Runtime,
and Linux continues to require the documented system GTK 3/WebKitGTK 4.1
runtime.
